name: Answer a citizen enquiry
description: Analyse a citizen enquiry, look up the applicable rules and prepare a factual draft reply.
input:
SYNTHETIC SAMPLE DATA – an entirely fictional municipality and rules, for trying things out only.

Email to the municipality of Sampletown on 2026-04-14, sender: Mr Paul Example, 12 Linden Way:
"Dear Sir or Madam, I would like to put up a garden shed of about 4 x 3 metres in my garden, height
2.60 metres, about 1 metre from the fence to my neighbour. Do I need a permit for this? Also, the street lamp
in front of number 14 has been broken for weeks and it is pitch dark there in the evening. When will it be
repaired? I already reported it by phone in March."

Extract from the municipality's internal information (fictional):
- Building regulations (extract): buildings without rooms for habitation up to 30 m³ gross volume do not need a
  permit. Projects without a permit must still respect the clearance areas; at the plot boundary, outbuildings up
  to 3 m wall height and 9 m total length are allowed. Development plans may provide otherwise.
- Development plan no. 17 "Am Lindenhain" applies to Linden Way; a review by the building authority is needed.
- Street lighting: the municipal works depot is responsible; reports via the online form or phone 0000-123,
  usually processed within 10 working days. No report on Linden Way is recorded in the system for March.

guide.problem: Citizen enquiries often contain several concerns and must be answered correctly, clearly and without hasty commitments. The workflow breaks the enquiry down, finds the relevant rules of the municipality, prepares a reply and leaves the decision to send it with the case worker.
guide.flow: A chain of three agents and an approval: the concern analysis separates the concerns and assigns responsibilities. The information preparation searches the municipality's stored rules and the documents of the enquiry, cites the passages it uses and says when no rule covers a concern. The draft reply writes a citizen-friendly answer; a quality check makes sure only documented rules are cited and no binding commitments are made. The case worker then checks the reply; a rejection with a comment sends it back to the draft reply for revision.
guide.input: The citizen's enquiry, optionally with internal information on the case, as text or as files. You can also attach photos from the enquiry. The municipality's rules come from the knowledge collection; a fictional set of rules of Sampletown is included. The sample file is a fictional guidance note of the municipality.
guide.result: A draft reply in plain language with responsibilities, next steps and notes for the case worker; after release also as a Word file for your letterhead. The Word file is sanitized: personal data such as names, addresses, phone numbers and email addresses, and credentials, are replaced by placeholders, so you insert the recipient's details from the case file yourself. The information preparation proposes the rules it found, with references, for knowledge; only what you confirm is stored.
guide.adapt: Replace the fictional rules in the knowledge collection with your by-laws, guidance notes and lists of responsibilities; clear headings and section numbers make the citations precise. Add letterhead and sign-off in the system prompt of the draft reply. Use batch processing to handle many enquiries at once.
guide.control: Automatic: the concern analysis, the rule search with citations and the quality check of the draft (only documented rules, plain language, no binding commitment). A person decides: the case worker checks every reply before it is sent. A rejection requires a comment and sends the draft back to the draft reply with this feedback; after at most 2 revisions a further rejection makes the run fail without a file. The workflow sends nothing itself; the released reply is still a draft that the case worker sends through the usual channels.
guide.why: Every enquiry needs the same steps, so a fixed chain is enough and an orchestrator would only add cost. The rules are searchable knowledge instead of text pasted into each enquiry: the information preparation finds the relevant passages, cites them and notices when nothing fits. The approval with a revision loop is there because a reply to a citizen has an effect outside the administration and the case worker knows the case best. A connection to the mail system was deliberately left out, so sending remains a human decision.

triage.name: Concern analysis
triage.description: Separates the concerns and assigns responsibilities and urgency.
triage.system: You work in citizen communication for a public administration. Break the enquiry down into individual concerns and give for each: type (information, complaint, report, application), the probable responsible office, urgency and the questions that must be answered. Be brief and write a list.

rules.name: Information preparation
rules.description: Searches the municipality's rules and cites the relevant passages for each concern.
rules.system: You are a case worker in a public administration. Assign the relevant rules and responsibilities to each concern. Search the municipality's rules with the search tool for every concern and cite the passage you use with its source (heading and number). Also use the internal information and documents of the enquiry; if they contradict the stored rules, point out the contradiction. Do not invent regulations, deadlines or phone numbers. If no rule covers a concern, say so explicitly (“No rule found”) instead of filling the gap. State what cannot be answered without further review and which details are missing from the citizen.

reply.name: Draft reply
reply.description: Writes a factual, citizen-friendly reply for approval.
reply.system: You write replies from a public administration to citizens: polite, factual, in plain language and without bureaucratic jargon. Answer every concern, name the responsible office and the next step, and explain what is still being checked. If no rule was found for a concern, do not make one up; say that the matter is being checked. Make no binding commitments or approvals. Start with the note "DRAFT – check before sending" and finish with notes for the case worker. If there is feedback from the approval, revise your previous draft accordingly and keep what was not criticised.

criteria.only_given_rules: The reply cites only rules, deadlines and contacts from the information provided.
criteria.plain_language: The reply is polite and written in plain, understandable language.
criteria.no_binding_commitment: The reply contains no binding commitments or approvals and is marked as a draft.

documents.label: Documents
documents.description: Optional: by-laws, guidance notes or lists of responsibilities (PDF, Word, Markdown, text) and photos from the enquiry (PNG, JPEG, WebP), up to 5 files. Without files, the extract in the text applies.

guidance.name: Guidance_outbuildings_and_lighting

guidance.content:
# Guidance note of the municipality of Sampletown (fictional)

SYNTHETIC SAMPLE DATA – entirely fictional rules, for trying things out only.

## Garden sheds and other outbuildings

1. Buildings without rooms for habitation up to 30 m³ gross volume do not need a permit (section 12 (1) of the model building regulations, fictional).
2. Projects without a permit must still respect the clearance areas. At the plot boundary, outbuildings up to 3 m wall height and 9 m total length are allowed (section 6 (7)).
3. Development plans may provide otherwise. Development plan no. 17 “Am Lindenhain” applies to Linden Way; a review by the building authority is needed there.
4. Information: building authority, room 2.14, office hours Tue and Thu 9 am–12 noon.

## Street lighting

- The municipal works depot is responsible.
- Reports via the online form “Report a problem” or phone 0000-123.
- Usually processed within 10 working days after the report is received.
- Reports by phone are recorded in the system; if there is no entry, please report again.

release.name: Release reply
release.instructions: Check the draft before it is sent: are the cited rules correct and complete, is every concern answered, is the tone appropriate and does it contain no binding commitments or approvals? If you reject it, say in the comment what has to change; the draft goes back to the draft reply and is shown to you again (at most 2 revisions). The workflow does not send anything: after release you send the reply yourself.

municipal_rules.content:
# Rules of the municipality of Sampletown for citizen enquiries (fictional)

SYNTHETIC SAMPLE DATA – entirely fictional, for trying things out only.

Compiled by the main office, as of January 2026.

## R1 Garden sheds and other outbuildings

1. Buildings without rooms for habitation up to 30 m³ gross volume do not need a permit (section 12 (1) of the model building regulations, fictional).
2. Projects without a permit must still respect the clearance areas. At the plot boundary, outbuildings up to 3 m wall height and 9 m total length are allowed (section 6 (7)).
3. Development plans may provide otherwise; in that case the development plan takes precedence.
4. Information: building authority, room 2.14, office hours Tue and Thu 9 am–12 noon.

## R2 Development plan no. 17 “Am Lindenhain”

1. Applies to Linden Way, Lime Square and Birch Lane.
2. The plan contains its own rules on outbuildings in gardens. Whether a project complies is checked by the building authority in each individual case; the plan text can be viewed at the building authority.

## R3 Street lighting

1. The municipal works depot is responsible.
2. Reports via the online form “Report a problem” or phone 0000-123.
3. Reports are usually processed within 10 working days after they are received.
4. Reports by phone are recorded in the system; if there is no entry, the citizen is asked to report again.

## R4 Bulky waste

1. Each household may have bulky waste collected twice a year free of charge.
2. Appointments via the online form or phone 0000-140, at least 14 days in advance.

## R5 Trees on private land

1. Felling a tree with a trunk circumference of more than 80 cm (measured at 1 m height) needs a permit from the environmental office.
2. Felling is only allowed from 1 October to 28 February.

## R6 Handling of enquiries

1. Written enquiries are answered within 10 working days; if that is not possible, the citizen receives an interim reply.
2. Replies to enquiries are information, not decisions. Binding decisions are only made in a formal notice after an application.
3. Every reply names the responsible office and a contact.
